o1.biggest_strength: It builds the three scripts around the real winning signals: 3 pm soda, blind taste test, family/game day, price objection, and taste before claims.
o1.biggest_mistake: The third script has a small label-reading beat that could feel less taste-led than the other two, even though it comes after the family reaction.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the paid disclosure note inside each individual creator brief and sharpen the family script so the taste/ranking moment carries more of the ad than the label moment.

o2.biggest_strength: It clearly uses the performance data to choose the angles and avoids the weak label-read and founder-story openings.
o2.biggest_mistake: It adds unnecessary assumptions and unfinished production terms, and the 'must say all approved claims' instruction conflicts with scripts that do not use all three claims in every ad.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the placeholders and extra assumptions, fix the disclosure wording for Meta and TikTok, and make the claim rules match the actual scripts.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 1 feels cleaner, more brand-safe, and more ready to send to creators without edits. Output 2 has useful production detail, but the contradictions and 'to confirm' loose ends make it slightly less finished.
